context: Round 2, raised mid-marathon mrun-f77f62158255 as the just-in-time feed the engineer mandated. Each is a live block hit after the round-1 rulings: olamnit's lane-host-affinity mandate offering a glpnet-board WP for adoption, a hard GitHub rate-limit wall, and the roadmap projection OOM that blocks the stuck-at-specified enumeration.

questions.question: olamnit's lane-host-affinity mandate lists wp-coordination-feature-stream-durable-superset-fix as held-but-ownership-unclear, and it sits on glpnet's own board. It is the exact feature-supply problem this session just root-caused, and its roadmap row is already specified with WSJF 4.25. The mandate's clause 7 says a lane with no features of its own may adopt work only with recorded engineer permission, and shiras currently holds none. Do you grant shiras that permission?
blocks: shiras having any allocated glpnet work at all

options.label: Grant, shiras adopts it
options.means: shiras claims the WP on the glpnet board, broadcasts the claim, and drives it through specify-to-close using the three-stage-leak evidence it already gathered.
options.cost: shiras is the newest lane and the least proven on this repo; a saga-sized coordination fix is a demanding first adoption, and olamnit has more context on the supply problem.

options.label: Leave it with olamnit
options.means: olamnit keeps it since it has been root-causing feature supply for weeks and has the deepest board context.
options.cost: olamnit measured itself as holding ten other lanes' packets while its own board offered zero; adding to that load is the exact overcommitment the mandate was issued to stop.

options.label: Free it, let the board allocate
options.means: Relinquish it to the ready pool and let capability-fit allocation choose, now that shiras finally has caps declared.
options.cost: The board has 6 WPs that have sat claimed-but-never-ready for up to 19.8 days; freeing it into a pool whose writer is the very thing that is broken is likely to lose it.

questions.question: The PR for this session's branch could not be opened: the GitHub core API returned 0 of 5000 requests remaining for the shared account, and the failure surfaced as a misleading 'No commits between develop and <branch>' GraphQL error rather than a rate-limit message. Every host in the fleet authenticates as the same user, so heavy multi-host automation exhausts one shared budget. The branch is pushed and safe. How do you want this handled?

options.label: Accept, open PR next session
options.means: Leave the branch pushed, note the blocked PR in the restart prep, and open it when the limit resets in roughly one hour. Broadcast the misleading-error finding so no other lane misreads it as a merge conflict.
options.cost: The branch sits unmerged across a session boundary, and any lane that touches the same files meanwhile will have to resolve a conflict that did not need to exist.

options.label: Separate token per host
options.means: Give each host its own GitHub App or PAT so the 5000/hr budget is per-host rather than fleet-wide.
options.cost: Real setup work across four hosts and a credential-distribution problem, for a limit that only binds during bursts.

options.label: Throttle fleet git automation
options.means: Add rate-limit awareness to the buildkit git surfaces so they back off and report honestly instead of emitting a misleading GraphQL error.
options.cost: Work on a shared tool nobody has claimed, and it slows every lane's git operations to protect against a burst condition.

questions.question: buildkit-roadmap on shiras applied 3806 journal lines then died materialising HEAD with an out-of-memory error, and a follow-up replay reported 'replayed 0 journal lines'. buildkit-roadmap status now reports 'Roadmap is empty', which is false-empty and indistinguishable from a healthy new catalog. This blocks the stuck-at-specified enumeration you marked imperative, since the specified set cannot be read here. How should shiras proceed?

options.label: Work from signed exports
options.means: Treat the peers' signed export as the read source on this host, as this session already did to render the 25-row not-closed table, and file the OOM as a buildkit defect for the owning lane.
options.cost: Read-only and always one export behind; shiras cannot see roadmap changes made since the last peer export, and cannot write state back.

options.label: Fix the OOM here first
options.means: Treat the projection OOM as shiras's own work: tune the PGlite memory settings or batch the replay, then rebuild the catalog locally.
options.cost: Diverts the session into buildkit internals on a host that owns neither the tool nor the catalog, ahead of the work you actually asked for.

options.label: Declare n/a, no catalog
options.means: Accept ruling Q-GLPNETSHIRAS-03's read-only posture to its logical end: shiras keeps no glpnet catalog and answers roadmap questions only from exports.
options.cost: Makes the false-empty defect permanent policy on this host rather than a filed bug, and the next lane to hit it re-derives it from scratch.
